state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's revisit the concept of range in this context. Remember, the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values in a set of data. Think about how cutting all the plant heights in half or adding \(3 \mathrm{~cm}\) to each height would affect the range. Can you explain your reasoning behind your choice of Tom as the one you agree with?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, so I thought Tom was right because if you cut all the plants in half, the range stays the same... but now I'm confused because if you add 3 cm to each plant, wouldn't that also keep the range the same since you're doing the same thing to all of them? Like, shouldn't both of them be right then?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's think about it this way: when you cut all the plants in half, the difference between the highest and lowest heights will still be the same because you're reducing all the values by the same proportion. However, when you add 3 cm to each height, you're actually increasing the range because the difference between the highest and lowest heights will now be greater. Can you see why Katie's reasoning makes more sense in this scenario?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher provides mathematically incorrect information (claiming proportional changes preserve range while additive changes increase it, when the opposite is true), fails to engage the student's emerging correct reasoning in Turn 2, and the student shows no improvement by the end.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses questioning and guided discovery rather than direct explanation with worked examples, and provides incorrect mathematical information (claiming adding a constant increases the range, when it actually keeps it constant), which contradicts the traditional strategy's emphasis on clear, direct instruction.
